## Verdict: no agent-facing context surface

The scan confirms it — `crime_00018`, charge **Missing Agent Context** (`missing_agent_context`, medium, confidence 0.90):

> "Repo ships no agent-readable instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md)."

Evidence the detector cites:
- no `AGENTS.md` at repo root
- no `CLAUDE.md` at repo root
- no `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- no `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`
- `package.json` declares bins `tsup`, `tsup-node` — **a published CLI with no documented entry points for agents**

That last line is the one that matters. This repo ships a binary other people depend on, and there is nothing in-tree telling an agent how to build it, how to test it, or what's load-bearing.

## What that costs you on your first PR

An agent (or a new human) landing here has to infer everything from the code, and the rest of the scan shows exactly where that inference goes wrong:

1. **No documented commands.** Nothing says how to run the build or the suite. An agent guesses `npm test`, or edits without running anything.
2. **The test suite gives false green.** 12 tests have **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls (`crime_00035`–`crime_00046`, e.g. `test/shims.test.ts:5` "removeNodeProtocol works on shims"), plus 14 more with only weak matchers. A passing run does not mean your change is safe, and nothing in the repo warns you of that. This is the single highest-value thing an AGENTS.md could say.
3. **No map of what's load-bearing.** `src/utils.ts` has fan-in 18, `src/plugin.ts` fan-in 10, `src/log.ts` fan-in 9 (`crime_00030`, `crime_00015`, `crime_00049`). `src/index.ts` has fan-out 17 and is 460 lines with a 293-line `build()` (`crime_00052`, `crime_00050`, `crime_00008`). An agent that "tidies up" `src/utils.ts` ripples into 29 files with tests that won't catch it.
4. **Names lie in specific, documented places.** `build()` and `buildAll()` in `src/index.ts` and `getRollupConfig()` in `src/rollup.ts` all read as pure but call `removeFiles` / `setSilent` (`crime_00033`, `crime_00072`, `crime_00053`). An agent reasoning from names alone will misjudge blast radius.

The compound effect is the actual risk: **confident-but-wrong edits in high-fan-in files, validated by tests that assert nothing.** That's not a hypothetical — every input to it is in this scan.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

The detector looks for any one of `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md`, or `.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md`. A root `AGENTS.md` is the portable choice (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor all read it). Verify the commands against `package.json` before committing — I've marked the ones to confirm:

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

`tsup` — bundle TypeScript libraries with esbuild. Published as the
`tsup` / `tsup-node` binaries. Breaking changes here break downstream builds.

## Commands

<!-- confirm each against package.json scripts before trusting -->
- Install:   `pnpm install`
- Build:     `pnpm build`
- Test:      `pnpm test`
- Typecheck: `pnpm typecheck`

Run build + test before proposing any change. Tests shell out to real
builds and are slow; expect minutes, not seconds.

## Layout

- `src/index.ts`        — public API; `build()` orchestrates the whole pipeline
- `src/cli-main.ts`     — CLI arg parsing and entry
- `src/esbuild/`        — esbuild runner and plugins (postcss, svelte, swc)
- `src/rollup.ts`       — .d.ts bundling via rollup
- `src/plugin.ts`       — plugin container / lifecycle hooks
- `src/utils.ts`        — shared helpers (imported nearly everywhere)
- `test/`               — integration tests; each spins up a real build

## Before you edit

**Load-bearing files — prefer additive changes, never restructure casually:**

| File | Why |
|---|---|
| `src/utils.ts` | 18 importers; touched by ~29 files transitively |
| `src/plugin.ts` | 10 importers; plugin lifecycle contract |
| `src/log.ts` | 9 importers |
| `src/index.ts` | 17 imports out; the pipeline hub |

**The test suite is weaker than it looks.** Several tests in
`test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`,
`test/tsconfig.test.ts`, and `test/experimental-dts.test.ts` run a build
but assert nothing. A green suite is *not* evidence your change is safe.
If you touch behaviour, add a real assertion — don't rely on existing coverage.

**These functions have side effects despite their names:**
- `build()` and `buildAll()` (`src/index.ts`) — delete files, create loggers
- `getRollupConfig()` (`src/rollup.ts`) — calls `removeFiles`, `setSilent`
- `buildStart()` (`src/rollup.ts`) — calls `removeFiles`

## Conventions

- Options flow through one wide `Options` bag; `normalizeOptions()`
  (`src/index.ts`) is the single place defaults are resolved. Add new
  options there, not at call sites.
- Plugins follow the esbuild plugin shape: `{ name, setup }`.
- Public API surface is `src/index.ts` exports — additions are semver-minor,
  signature changes are semver-major.
```

That's ~50 lines and it clears `crime_00018` outright. If you want it to earn its place beyond the finding, the "test suite is weaker than it looks" section is the part that will actually save someone's afternoon — it encodes a fact no amount of reading the code will surface, because the tests *look* comprehensive right up until you count the assertions.

Two notes on scope: this clears the *context* finding only. The 9 high-severity findings (five God Functions, `docs/README.md` at 679 lines) remain — the AGENTS.md just makes them navigable rather than fixed. And the detector only checks for file presence, so a stub would technically clear it; the version above is written to be worth reading, which is the actual point.
